name: post price undercuts the cheapest other auction unless the median is lower
why: 55c - 1c = 54c, below the 60c level (an ask level, its own ceiling)

name: post price stops at the 7-day median
why: 70c - 1c = 69c is above the 60c level (an ask level, its own ceiling)

name: post price without competition is the median
why: nothing else listed

name: post price without a median undercuts
why: no history yet

name: no post price without either
why: nothing to go by: flagged no price

name: post price undercuts up to the ceiling, this hour's forecast of the level
why: min(129c, floor(100c x 1.10 + 0.5) = 110c): the sold level with the hour's pattern is the cap

name: post price is the undercut when it is under the ceiling
post price without competition is the ceiling
why: nobody else listed: this hour's forecast, 110c

name: the ceiling stops at the high bound
why: 100c x 1.80 = 180c is lowered to the high bound 150c, the larger of the curve's 90th and the level

name: an ask level is its own ceiling
why: an ask level's high bound is itself: 77c x 1.20 = 92c is lowered to 77c, under the 1s 99c undercut

name: the ceiling follows a quiet hour down
why: floor(77c x 0.90 + 0.5) = floor(69.8) = 69c, inside [50c, 77c]

name: without a level the undercut is uncapped
why: no level: PP1's rule, 55c - 1c

name: no post price without a level or a competitor
why: nothing to go by: flagged no price

name: the ceiling rounds half up before the bounds
why: 77c x 0.5 = 38.5c rounds half up to 39c; without bounds (a level never lacks them in a document) nothing clamps it

name: a relist into an empty book on thin data has no price
why: the Spaulders: their only listing is the one bought, and an ask level of 150g from 4 closes grounds nothing

name: a relist into an empty book with 30 closes is the level
why: 30 >= 24 hourly closes ground the level: post_price without a competitor is the ceiling, 150g

name: a relist under a listing left is grounded on thin data
why: Linen at 10c and 50c: the 50c listing grounds the undercut, min(49c, the ceiling 55c) = 49c

name: a relist with an unknown close count is the post price
why: an unknown count is not thin (as PF30)

name: a rising trend stops at +15% in total
a falling trend stops at -15% in total
a trend inside the clamp is unchanged
a window forecast from the level inside its bounds
why: a sold level of 100c with the curve's bounds 80c and 150c: 100c x 1.2 = 120c, inside them

name: a window forecast stops at the high bound
why: 200c is lowered to the high bound: a window can't promise more than the dearest tenth of sales went for

name: a window forecast is raised to the low bound
why: 50c is raised to the low bound 80c, the curve's 10th

name: under 20 units the level is the ceiling
why: a sold level of 12 units has no curve: the bounds are p10_30 60c and the level, so 120c is lowered to 100c

name: under 20 units the floor is p10_30
why: 50c is raised to p10_30, 60c

name: an ask level is its own ceiling
why: an ask level of 77c with p10_30 50c: 92c is lowered to 77c (thin data's rule, TT23's, now for every level that is only asks)

name: an ask level's forecast is raised to p10_30
why: floor(38.5 + 0.5) = 39c is raised to the low bound 50c

name: a lone low bound still raises the forecast
why: 100c x 0.805 = 80.5c rounds half up to 81c, then is raised to the low bound 85c; no high bound to lower it
